name: GoesMagnetometer
description: One-minute averaged magnetometer readings from a GOES spacecraft, published by the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center. Derived from the noaa-goes feeder schema published in the xRegistry catalogue. The sample exists because `he`, `hp` and `hn` are the three components of one vector quantity resolved in a spacecraft-local frame, and nothing but the accompanying documentation says so: `hp` is parallel to the Earth's dipole axis and positive northward, `hn` lies along the spacecraft-Earth line and is positive earthward, and `he` completes the triad perpendicular to both and is positive eastward. It demonstrates a calculated magnitude alongside the measured components it is computed from, observingProcedure on the spacecraft rather than on a site, and resultQuality carried by a boolean that marks the readings as contaminated by the spacecraft's own thrusters. The frame in which the components are resolved is stated in prose here, because the coordinate reference system annotation binds the members that give a position and not the members that give the components of a vector.

time_tag.description: UTC instant labelling the one-minute averaging window, from the `time_tag` field. The feed publishes one record per minute per spacecraft.

satellite.description: GOES spacecraft number, from the `satellite` field, for example 19. It identifies the instrument and, with it, the frame the components are resolved in and the longitude the spacecraft is stationed at, so records from two satellites are not interchangeable even when their timestamps agree.

hp.description: Component of the magnetic field parallel to the Earth's dipole axis, positive northward, from the `hp` field. It is the component the operational indices are built from, and under quiet conditions at geostationary altitude it sits between roughly 80 and 120 nT; a sharp drop marks the compression of the magnetopause by a solar wind pressure increase.

hn.description: Component of the magnetic field along the spacecraft-Earth line, positive radially earthward, from the `hn` field.

he.description: Component of the magnetic field perpendicular to both the spacecraft-Earth line and the dipole axis, positive eastward, from the `he` field. The letter is not a chemical symbol; it names the eastward member of the triad.

total.description: Magnitude of the field vector, from the `total` field, computed by the publisher as the root of the sum of the squares of `he`, `hp` and `hn`. It is not an independent reading and adds no information to the three components, but it is frame-invariant where they are not, so it is the member to compare across spacecraft. Quiet-time values at geostationary altitude lie between roughly 100 and 120 nT.

arcjet_flag.description: True when the spacecraft's electric propulsion thrusters were firing during the averaging window, from the `arcjet_flag` field. A firing thruster generates a magnetic field at the sensor that is indistinguishable from a geophysical signal, so a flagged record reports the instrument's environment rather than the magnetosphere and must be excluded from analysis rather than corrected.
